newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues CS First Boston over Orange County bonds.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues CS First Boston over Orange County bonds.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday that it sued CS First Boston Corp. and two of its former investment bankers for fraud in the offer and sale of Orange County, Calif., bonds.
SEC officials in Los Angeles said the lawsuit was part of the regulatory agency's ongoing investigation of the Orange County bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.

Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. It was the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
CS First Boston is a unit of CS Holding, a Swiss banking and financial services company. The SEC filed its complaint in U.S. District Court in Santa Ana, Calif.

The SEC said it is seeking permanent injunctions and unspecified civil penalties against CS First Boston, a broker-dealer headquartered in New York, and the former investment bankers, identified as Jerry Nowlin and Douglas Montague.
In its complaint the SEC alleged fraud in the offer and sale of $110 million of Series B pension obligation bonds issued by Orange County in September 1994.

The complaint alleged that while participating in the drafting and preparing of the county's bond offering documents CS First Boston and the two bankers "knew, or were reckless in not knowing, significant negative information about the county (investment) pools that was misrepresented in or omitted from the official statement."
